neighbours.label: The opening word ('If', 'let's say') of a question being posed: fires right after a line that announces or sets up a question, not on a narrative 'If'
fire: Here is the question my neighbor keeps asking: "If the fence falls on my side, who pays for it?"
Parents often write to me with this question: "If my son skips breakfast, will he do worse at school?"
Now I want to ask you something. If your boss offered you a raise, would you take it?
I had one more question for the mayor. If the budget is so tight, why build a stadium?
Q. What is your favorite meal? A. Soup. Q. If you could eat only one food, what would it be?
The interviewer leaned forward and asked a question: "If you were president, what would you change first?"
But let's say a customer asked you, "Where does this coffee come from?"
That has me wondering: if the moon vanished tomorrow, what would happen to the tides?
quiet: The fence fell on my side during the storm. If it rains again, the yard will flood.
My son skipped breakfast this morning. If he eats late, he usually feels fine by noon.
My boss gave me a raise last month. If sales keep growing, the whole team gets one too.
The mayor spoke about the budget. If it passes, the stadium will open in two years.
Soup is my favorite meal. If you heat it slowly, the flavor gets stronger.
The president changed the policy last year. If you were there, you saw the crowd cheer.
A customer bought our coffee yesterday and said that it comes from Peru.
The moon looked huge last night. If the sky stays clear, it will look the same tomorrow.

notes: Promotes ' What'/'Could'/' please'. Probes: announced 'If' 0.70-0.79, narrative 'If' 0.04-0.15.
